back: Multiply each digit by its place value (… 64, 8, 1) and add.
Divide by 8 repeatedly; read the remainders (0-7) from the bottom up.
Each octal digit = **3 bits** (0 = 000 … 7 = 111). Group binary in threes from the right.
Octal: base 8, 3 bits per digit, no letters. Hex: base 16, 4 bits per digit, a byte = exactly 2 digits, so hex is more common.
File permissions on some operating systems (e.g. 7 = 111 = read, write, execute).
An octal number never contains 8 or 9; a remainder of 8 or more means a division slip.
